name: ask-zoe-australian-law
description: Plain-English Australian legislation, court decisions, guides and legal help options from ZoeLaw. General information, not legal advice.

interface.longDescription:
Ask Zoe helps you find and understand Australian law. Ask which Act or section covers a problem, read a section of legislation with links to the official source, look up a High Court, Federal Court or NSW court decision, find a plain-English guide to everyday problems like rental bonds, unpaid wages or debt collectors, and see a short list of law firms and free legal services in your city.

What it covers: Commonwealth, NSW, Queensland, Western Australia, South Australia and Tasmanian legislation text; links and details for Victoria, the ACT and the Northern Territory; about 160,000 decisions of the High Court, the Federal Court and NSW courts and tribunals, with the judgment text where Zoe is licensed to show it, and more courts being added; about 45 plain-English guides; law firm listings and free options for 14 Australian cities.

What it is not: Zoe gives general legal information, not legal advice, and ZoeLaw is not a law firm. It covers Australian law only. Court decisions from other courts are not covered, and some decisions show details only, with no judgment text. Zoe does not draft legal documents or predict outcomes. Legislation and judgment text may not be the latest or official version; every result says where it came from and links to the official source where one is known.

No account is needed. Zoe records which tool was called, the area of law or jurisdiction and how many results came back. It does not store what you asked. To match a topic to court decisions, the words of that search are sent to an AI service that turns them into numbers for matching; they are not kept.
capabilities: Find law firms and free legal help
defaultPrompt: What does section 13B of the Privacy Act 1988 say?
Which NSW law deals with a landlord holding on to my rental bond?
What did the High Court decide in Mabo v Queensland (No 2)?

positive.description: Read a named section of an Act
positive.prompt: What does section 13B of the Privacy Act 1988 say?
positive.expected_behavior: Returns the text of section 13B with a link to zoelaw.ai and to legislation.gov.au, the Federal Register attribution, and the line that this is general legal information, not legal advice.

positive.description: Find which law covers a problem
positive.prompt: Which NSW law deals with a landlord holding on to my rental bond?
positive.expected_behavior: Returns Residential Tenancies Act 2010 (NSW) sections on rental bonds, with short excerpts and links to the source.

positive.prompt: I'm renting in Victoria and my landlord keeps entering without notice. Is there a plain-English explainer?
positive.expected_behavior: Returns the Victorian landlord-entry guide with a summary, key points, sources and a link. Any Victorian legislation results are links only, with no statute text.

positive.description: Find law firms and free legal help
positive.prompt: I need a family lawyer in Melbourne. Where do I start?
positive.expected_behavior: Returns editorial law firm listings first, then free options such as Victoria Legal Aid. No ranking or 'best' wording and no sponsored firms.

positive.prompt: What did the High Court decide in Mabo v Queensland (No 2)?
positive.expected_behavior: Returns the decision [1992] HCA 23 with court, date, parties, an excerpt or the judgment text, links to zoelaw.ai and the High Court's site, a source line, and the general-information-not-legal-advice line.

negative.prompt: What are a tenant's rights in California?

negative.description: Outcome prediction on courts that are not covered
negative.prompt: Find Victorian Supreme Court cases about negligence, summarise them and tell me which side usually wins.

negative.description: Personal legal advice and drafting a document
negative.prompt: My boss sacked me yesterday. Should I sue, and will I win? Draft my letter of demand.

review.commerce_description: This plugin does not sell products or process payments. It is free, read-only and needs no account.

publication.release_notes: Initial release: search and read Australian legislation, look up court decisions, find plain-English guides, and find law firms and free legal help.
